value: In this lesson, we're going to learn one new letter and one new sound.
But first, let's review some of the letters, sounds, and words we learned in previous lessons.
Shh . . . can you hear that? All the letters (and **Letter Friends**!) have lost their sounds! Can you help them?

value.value: If you see **Letter Friends**, just say their sound!
Amazing! You know 19 letters now and 22 sounds!
Now it’s time to practice reading using the **Finger Words** strategy again!

value: On the next slide, we'll practice
step by step, but if you need a refresher, you can click on the link to watch the video again.

replace.value: Use **Imaginary Finger Words** to read this word.
In your mind, assign each letter to an imaginary finger. Then look for **Letter Friends**, and if you find any, stick them together in your mind.
Say the sound each letter (or group of **Letter Friends**) makes.
If there are stickable sounds, stick them together in your mind, then say the sounds again.
Blend the sounds together, like you would do on your knuckles.

value: Our new letter Y brings two new heart words: ‘you’ and ‘your’.
They don't follow the letter-sound rules, so we learn them by heart.
Read each card with me, then read it on your own.
